newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Siemens power unit sees flat sales, profit.
newsitem.headline: Siemens power unit sees flat sales, profit.

text.p: The KWU power generation division of German conglomerate Siemens AG expects to post steady sales and profit in the year to September 30, division chief Adolf Huettl told journalists on Thursday.

Siemens is not planning to spin off the unit, which posted a profit of 410 million marks ($238 million) in 1995/96, Huettl said, but he declined to comment on reports of planned cooperation with Westinghouse. ($ = 1.722 German Marks)
"There is no plan to divide KWU in parts, to prepare it for some sort of eventualities," he said.

The power-plant market remains stagnant in industrialised nations, and prices continue to subside, putting pressure on results, Huettl said. KWU continues to work with France's Framatome on the joint development of a new model nuclear power plant.
KWU, which was Siemens's fourth most profitable division last year, had incoming orders of 9.1 billion marks and sales of 8.0 billion marks.
The division has been reducing its personnel for several years, but should remain stable at the current 19,000 in the coming year, Huettl said. The German workforce should also remain stable.

Basic planning for the European pressurised reactor (EPR) KWU is jointly developing with Framatome should be completed this summer. Siemens and German utilities hope to secure a new form of approval for the reactor as a type, without specifying a site for its planned construction.
Nuclear power oversight authorities from several German states, but especially Siemens's home state of Bavaria, are taking an interest in the project, he said.

No new nuclear plant has been completed in Germany in over 10 years, partly due to strong popular opposition and partly to energy conservation efforts that reduce the need for additional power supply.
